title: 7 Viggle AI alternatives for character animation (2026)
summary: Compare 7 Viggle AI alternatives in 2027 for character animation, motion transfer, and video character replacement. Find the right tool for your workflow.
body_markdown:
You want to replace or animate a character in a clip, but you’re not sure which Viggle alternative fits the result you have in mind. A tool for stylized animation may not solve the same problem as one built around a recorded performance or a specific export workflow. Switching without making that distinction can leave you with another tool that misses the job.


This guide compares seven alternatives by what you can start with, the controls you need and the result you want to finish. You’ll also see what Viggle already supports, so you can decide whether to switch at all. Choose a workflow first, then compare the same shot before committing.


## Quick answer


**Start with**


[Magic Hour Character Replace](https://magichour.ai/products/character-replace) **for a no-account character-replacement trial.**


Compare Runway Act-Two for a recorded performance with speech, or DomoAI for stylized animation. Viggle already supports replacing people in existing clips, so switch for a specific workflow or control you need.


### Replace a character in a video


Upload a source video and character image, then review the replacement in Magic Hour.


[Try Character Replace](https://magichour.ai/products/character-replace)


## What Viggle AI Supports Now


[Viggle’s current guide](https://viggle.ai/blog/viggle-ai-the-ultimate-guide) distinguishes **Mix** , which replaces a character in a video, from **Motion Control** (formerly Move), which animates a still character using movement from a video. Multi supports multiple character replacements, and Editor adds selection and tracking controls.


Both Magic Hour and Viggle offer character replacement. When comparing them, use the same reference image and source footage, then inspect identity, body movement, background changes and the final export. Matching the input workflow makes that comparison meaningful; a text-to-video demo does not establish replacement quality.


Viggle supports uploaded motion references and templates. Its[Free plan](https://viggle.ai/pricing) lists five videos per day for signed-in users. Daily allowance, concurrency, upload length and retained assets are separate limits, so compare the one that is preventing you from finishing your project.


You can use Viggle through the web, iOS and Android; its official guide also lists Discord. A Discord-free workflow is therefore not, by itself, a reason to switch.


### Before switching: check Viggle’s current controls


For difficult character references,[Viggle’s V4 guide](https://viggle.ai/blog/everything-you-need-is-in-viggle-v4) documents Character Refine, Smooth Motion and Foot Lock. Character Refine builds multiple-angle references from an uploaded image; the guide also describes multi-track selection for replacing several characters. These are documented controls, not proof that every motion, identity or background will remain correct.


Match the control to the problem. If the reference changes appearance during a turn, prepare a clearer reference and examine identity through that turn. If the wrong person changes in group footage, compare subject selection and tracking. If feet slide, inspect foot contact and motion recovery. Do not switch tools because one convenient preview looks better; compare the completed clips from the same source.


For billing or upload constraints, use[Viggle’s current plan table](https://viggle.ai/pricing) separately: it lists a one-minute Free upload maximum, one simultaneous generation and seven-day asset storage. Those are different limits from the five-videos-per-day allowance. Check the selected feature and account before preparing a larger project.


## Viggle API: motion transfer, masks and 3D assets


Automation alone does not require switching providers. Viggle publishes a[developer API](https://viggle.ai/developers) for Mix/Remix motion transfer, Viggle-Animate character replacement and additional workflows. Its Mix/Remix flow reuses Character and Motion resources and can return a rendered video plus a separate alpha-mask video for compositing.


Define the deliverable before comparing alternatives: a rendered character clip, an alpha mask and a rigged 3D character are different assets. Viggle’s pricing page bills its PINOC 3D product separately from Viggle AI plans, and lists a separate pay-as-you-go API offer. Do not treat a consumer video subscription as a bundled 3D-export or API balance. A finished MP4 does not establish an editable 3D handoff. Check the exact operation, inputs, result retrieval and API billing before integrating a batch; a web subscription or demonstration does not by itself verify those API entitlements. See the[official API documentation](https://docs.viggle.ai/) .

A free preview is useful only if it lets you evaluate the part that matters. For character replacement, download the result and inspect motion, identity and the background. For production, also check the license, watermark, resolution and cost of another attempt.


## **The 7 Best Viggle AI Alternatives**


### **1. Magic Hour**


**Best for:** Replacing a character in existing footage with a real person, cartoon, or anime character


[Magic Hour Character Replace](https://magichour.ai/products/character-replace) takes an existing video and replaces the main person while preserving the original movement, timing, background, and camera work. It works in the browser without Discord, an app download, or an account just to try the free product flow. You can also use real people, cartoon characters, anime characters, and illustrated references.


The live interface shows **Replace** and **Animate** . The no-account tool offers three free generations per day; check the current uploader and generation quote for supported length and settings. Test a clear single-subject shot first, then move to difficult turns or occlusion. Avoid assuming that a preview’s settings apply to every paid workflow.


**Access:** browser trial without an account. Paid Magic Hour subscriptions and credit-pack purchases include commercial-use rights and watermark-free video exports. Packs do not unlock every subscriber-only setting. See[current plans](https://magichour.ai/pricing) ; the annual monthly equivalent and month-to-month charge are different prices.


### Watch the replacement and animation routes


This official Magic Hour walkthrough demonstrates replacing a person in footage and animating a reference image. Match the recorded route to your starting input, then review the full result for changes to the subject and scene. Current modes and controls can differ from the recording.


Source:[Magic Hour AI: How to Replace a Person in a Video & Animate Any Image with AI | Magic Hour](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eS3dqwxowvY)


### Try the exact character-replacement workflow


To put a new character into footage you already have, open[Magic Hour Character Replace](https://magichour.ai/products/character-replace) and supply a source video plus replacement image. The source supplies the performance; the image supplies the new appearance. Choose Replace when the source setting should stay. Choose Animate when the reference image should follow the recorded movement.


Choose the model and mode first in the[signed-in Character Replace workflow](https://magichour.ai/create/character-replace) . The[step-by-step Help Center guide](https://help.magichour.ai/en/articles/16917099-character-replace-step-by-step-guide) makes this model-dependent: manual Select person is available with MiniMax H3 in Replace person, while Kling 3.0 targets automatically. Confirm Select This Person on a clear frame when offered, and recheck points after trimming. Review the completed clip before downloading.


If only facial identity should change while hair, clothing and body remain, use[Face Swap Video](https://magichour.ai/products/face-swap/video) instead. A saved Characters reference helps reuse an identity; it is not itself a replacement operation.


### **2. Kling AI**


**Best fit:** reference motion with character-orientation and identity controls.


[Kling Motion Control](https://kling.ai/quickstart/motion-control-user-guide) applies an uploaded performance or a library motion to a character image. The guide documents orientation choices and VIDEO 3.0 identity controls. Match full-body or half-body framing between the image and motion reference, and start with one continuously visible subject.


The VIDEO 3.0 Motion Control rate table lists **9 credits/second for Standard** and **12 for Professional** , with duration rounded to the nearest second. A 10-second attempt is therefore 90 or 120 Kling credits. That is a usage calculation, not a dollar price or a promise that your free balance includes the feature.


**Tradeoff:** rapid action, cuts and occlusion can reduce the usable motion segment. Check the selected model’s input rules and the in-app quote; a generic subscription starting price does not tell you the cost of this workflow.


### **3. DomoAI**


**Best for:** Anime and stylized 2D character animation


[DomoAI](https://www.domoai.app/) is particularly useful when the character's visual style matters as much as its movement. It supports anime, illustration, realistic, and other stylized workflows, with dedicated character-animation and image-to-video tools. Our[DomoAI review](https://magichour.ai/blog/domoai-review) covers its video-to-anime workflow, plan limits, Fast and Relax modes, lip sync, and enterprise API.


The[current pricing page](https://www.domoai.app/pricing) displays Basic at **$9/month billed annually** , with **600 monthly credits** and watermark-free outputs. Basic and Standard list 5- and 10-second Character to Video; Pro adds 20- and 30-second outputs. Confirm the checkout total and billing period before purchase.


**Tradeoff:** Relax Mode is limited to eligible plans and models. Longer character outputs use Fast Mode; “unlimited” does not mean every model, duration or priority level is included. The help center describes a 15-credit trial, which is a starting balance rather than a guaranteed finished video.


### **4. Runway**


**Best for:** Professional creators building character animation into a larger production workflow


[Runway Act-Two](https://help.runwayml.com/hc/en-us/articles/42311337895827-Performance-Capture-with-Act-Two) transfers a driving performance to a character image or video. It supports clips up to 30 seconds at **5 credits per second** , with a three-second minimum charge. Image inputs enable gesture control; video inputs preserve the character video’s scene and motion while transferring facial performance. Select the input type that matches your shot.


Match input durations before budgeting an Act-Two shot. Runway says a character video shorter than the driving performance is repeated with a reversed “boomerang” effect to fill the performance. For example (illustrative), pairing an eight-second performance with a four-second character video can introduce reversed movement during the finished shot. Use a character video close to the performance’s length when the recorded camera and scene motion matter. A character image is another option, but Act-Two adds environmental motion to image inputs. Watch for reversal and unwanted camera movement before accepting the result.


Runway Standard is $15 monthly or $144/year with 625 monthly credits; Pro is $35 or $336/year with 2,250; Max is $95 or $912/year with 9,500. Max is a credit allocation, not the earlier unlimited-plan promise. Web and API billing are separate. See[current Runway pricing](https://magichour.ai/blog/runway-ml-pricing) .


### **5. Higgsfield**


**Best fit:** changing characters, objects or environments within existing footage.


[Higgsfield Genjutsu](https://higgsfield.ai/blog/higgsfield-genjutsu) offers Motion Transfer and Object Swap. It accepts one 4–30-second source clip and up to 30 reference images, with output up to 1080p. Use Motion Transfer for a character or scene driven by the performance; use Object Swap to target an element such as a prop or outfit.


The official guide lists a 15-second generation at **40 credits for 480p** , **104 for 720p** and **144 for 1080p** . Those are Higgsfield credits, not comparable one-for-one with Kling or Runway credits. Use the current Generate-button quote for the selected settings.


**Tradeoff:** Higgsfield’s[credit guide](https://higgsfield.ai/creator-hub/help-center/credits/how-credits-work) describes plan-specific free or unlimited generations, not universal free access to every model. Website allowances do not automatically cover MCP, CLI or other automated generation.


### **6. Luma AI**


**Best fit:** reference-guided modification and shot control.


[Luma Ray3.2](https://lumalabs.ai/ray) supports video modification, performance transfer and multiple keyframes, alongside text-to-video and image-to-video. Modify accepts up to **20 seconds at 24 fps** , **15 at 30 fps** or **7 at 60 fps** . It is a relevant option for transforming existing footage, not only generating a new environment.


Luma Plus is $30 monthly or $300/year with 10,000 monthly credits. Pro is $90 monthly with 40,000, and Ultra is $300 monthly with 150,000. Plus lists commercial use. Check trial access in your account and the terms that apply when you generate. See[current Luma pricing](https://magichour.ai/blog/luma-dream-machine-pricing) .


**Tradeoff:** choose the correct workflow before comparing limits or costs. At 720p, Luma lists 360 credits for a five-second Modify result; that differs from text/image-to-video generation. Our[Luma Dream Machine review](https://magichour.ai/blog/luma-dream-machine-review) explains the current cost and output distinctions.


### **7. MyEdit**


**Best for:** Beginners who want the dancing-photo trend in a simpler interface


[MyEdit Character Motion Swap](https://myedit.online/en/video-editor/wan-2-2-animate) runs Wan 2.2 Animate in the browser. **Keep the photo background** animates the still image; **Keep the video background** replaces the character within the clip. This choice is the relevant distinction for a Viggle user, rather than MyEdit’s general photo-editing features.


MyEdit’s tool page lists daily free credits and watermark-free results. In CyberLink’s[August workflow example](https://www.cyberlink.com/blog/trending-topics/5091/wan-2-2) , the quote was three credits per second, with an 18-credit charge for a 5.8-second result. Treat that as the vendor’s documented example; use the estimate in your account for your own clip.


**Tradeoff:** preserving movement does not establish likeness. Match the subject framing in both inputs and inspect facial details after generation. A daily credit allowance may be smaller than the cost of the clip you want.


## **Which One Should You Use?**


Start with **Magic Hour** when you want to try a character replacement without an account. Choose **Kling** for its motion-reference controls, **DomoAI** for stylized character workflows, **Runway Act-Two** for a performed scene, **Higgsfield Genjutsu** for targeted changes to existing footage, **Luma Ray3.2** for reference-guided modification and keyframes, or **MyEdit** for its explicit photo-background/video-background choice. These recommendations follow documented controls, not a measured quality ranking.


## Viggle vs Magic Hour: credits and occasional client work


**For occasional projects, compare unused credits as well as the starting price.** As checked October 6, 2026,[Viggle’s pricing FAQ](https://viggle.ai/pricing) says monthly plan credits expire on the billing date. Purchased credits do not expire, but using them requires an active Viggle subscription. That matters if you create several clips for a campaign, then pause.


[Magic Hour pricing](https://magichour.ai/pricing) says unused account credits roll over without expiration. A credit pack provides watermark-free exports and commercial-use rights. Subscriptions add benefits such as higher export resolutions, faster queues and larger uploads. Choose around your required deliverable rather than assuming a top-up unlocks every subscription feature.


For a client project, start with a short sample in[Character Replace](https://magichour.ai/products/character-replace) . Choose Replace when the original video’s scene must remain; choose Animate when you want a character image to follow movement from the video. Approve the actual downloaded sample before extending the job, then confirm export settings, remaining balance and purchase terms.


[Magic Hour’s Terms of Service](https://magichour.ai/terms-of-service) permit commercial output use for customers with a subscription, credit-pack purchase or separately agreed paid usage-based arrangement. You still need rights to the footage, music and likenesses. This comparison concerns billing flexibility and delivery requirements; it does not establish better motion or likeness for either platform.


## Compare the Same Shot Before Switching


Magic Hour publishes this guide and is included as an alternative. We selected active tools that replace or animate characters through materially different workflows, then compared documented inputs, controls, plan boundaries, and exports. This is not a retained identical-clip quality benchmark; current product sources are linked throughout.


Use the[motion-control comparison brief](https://magichour.ai/blog/best-ai-motion-control-tools) to check face stability, gesture timing and scene preservation on the same short performance before changing platforms.


Use a clear five-second source clip and one reference character. Try one straightforward gesture first, followed by a turn or brief hand-to-face occlusion. These are suggested checks, not tests we claim to have run.


- **Identity:** does the face and outfit remain recognizable through the whole shot?
- **Motion:** does the replacement follow the source timing without slipping hands or feet?
- **Scene:** does the selected background stay intact, including objects near the subject?
- **Delivery:** does the downloaded file have the required resolution, audio and watermark status?
- **Cost:** record all attempt charges, then divide total spend by clips you would actually publish.


If you are building a series, prepare consistent references first. Our[character-consistency guide](https://magichour.ai/blog/best-ai-image-generators-for-character-consistency) explains saved characters and a reusable reference sheet. Assemble the approved clips, sound and captions before evaluating the finished video.


## **A Note on Responsible Use**


Only use another person's photo as a character reference when you have their permission or are creating content featuring your own likeness. Do not create replacement or animation content that falsely presents a real person as saying or doing something they did not actually do. Check each platform's current terms before using generated content in a commercial or public-facing project.


## **What to Try Next**


If you want to replace a character in existing footage, follow our guide on[how to replace a character in a video with AI](https://magichour.ai/blog/how-to-replace-a-character-in-a-video-with-ai-for-free) to see the full Magic Hour workflow step by step.
For face-only swaps where you want to change someone's face without replacing their entire character, try[Magic Hour Face Swap Video](https://magichour.ai/products/face-swap/video) .
Both tools follow the same basic idea of transforming an existing video while preserving the original footage and movement, but they are designed for different types of replacements.


If you are moving from a Summrs template, use our[Summrs AI alternatives guide](https://magichour.ai/blog/summrs-ai-alternatives) to decide whether you need a new face, a whole character, the same performance or a broader scene edit. That distinction helps you choose between Face Swap Video, Character Replace and motion-transfer tools.


## Separate motion transfer from finished-video production


**Direct answer:** Viggle alternatives divide into motion-transfer tools, character-animation systems and broader video workspaces. The best choice depends on whether you need one dancing character, repeatable identity, scene editing or a complete deliverable.


**Test the hard frames.** Use a clip with footwork, a body turn, crossed limbs and a brief occlusion. Check hands, feet, silhouette, clothing, face identity and recovery after the subject reappears. Review at normal speed and frame by frame.


**Measure production cost.** Record preparation time, generation attempts, manual cleanup, export limits and accepted outputs. A fast first preview can still be expensive if the last five percent requires multiple tools.


**Decision rule.** Choose a specialist when motion transfer is the entire job. Choose a broader workflow when you also need source-image creation, face replacement, restyling, captions, sound or multiple model options.


**For restyling existing footage, try**[Magic Hour Video-to-Video](https://magichour.ai/products/video-to-video) . Start with a short clip and compare motion, character details and flicker; choose a motion-transfer tool when you need a different performance.
